title: Concurrency
description: Threads, locks, and coordinating work in Java

exercises.title: thread
exercises.description: Launch Java sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let thread run.
hints: Start `new Thread(() -> sayHello(done)).start();` use `CountDownLatch` so `main` can exit after child prints.

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch = a queue. Send "ping" to ch in thread, receive and System.out.println.

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and System.out.println both.
hints: Capacity-2 queue; `put(10)`, `put(20)`, then print both values taken.

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in thread after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.
hints: Second thread `sleep`s then `put` on the queue; main blocks on `take`.

exercises.title: Channel Close
exercises.description: Create channel, send 1,2,3 then close. Use range to receive until closed.
hints: Producer thread puts `1,2,3`; consumer loop `take`s three times printing each.

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Create two threads that each send a string to a shared channel. Use a third thread to fan-in (read) from the channel and System.out.println received values. Close the channel when both senders are done.
hints: Two threads `put` `"hello"` and `"world"`; main reads twice (order may follow start order in sample).

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 threads that each System.out.println their number, then wait for all to complete before System.out.printlning "done".
hints: Sequential `start/join` per iteration or `CountDownLatch` for three tasks; print `1\\n2\\n3\\ndone`.
